sql.description: The Truvio Commerce brand catalogue for SHOP1/ENU/EUR: 4 top groups x 3 subgroups (16 EcomGroups), 60 masters TCPROD0001..0060 with SKU TC-<CONCEPT>-<nnnn>, the Tier and Mode variant axes on 6 masters, BOUND to those masters through EcomVariantGroupProductRelation (the table that says which axes a product uses, and the one whose absence rendered every variant selector as an empty div while every other count was correct), with 36 combination rows, each with its own EcomPrices row, 1 BOM kit with 2 slots, 2 services, a 3-step quantity-tier ladder, one contract price scoped to customer number TC-100200, 4 product categories x 7 category fields with 180 populated values, a long description on every master (the PDP Overview band reads ProductLongDescription), and the tc_specs field display group over all 28 category fields, each named in the category-field reference form ProductCategory|<FieldCategoryId>|<FieldId> so the group actually resolves, which is what surface-swift's PDP spec table binds to. It also moves every currency row still carrying the placeholder rate 1 to 100. Every name is drawn from PIM/Commerce/CMS vocabulary (owner decision D-B); every key is TC*-prefixed and disjoint from sample-data's FIXT* and the feature families' PACK*.

The brand identities and their order history: the B2B account 100100 'Truvio Demo Account' (customer number TC-100200), the three personas 100101 buyer@ / 100102 csr@ / 100103 admin@ on the fictional truvio-demo domain, their memberships into the account and into the base-contract permission groups 1325 / 1292 / 1270, and 12 orders TCO-0001..TCO-0012 (20 lines) across the OrderFlowId 1 states New / Completed / Rejected. Runs after the deserialize rather than before host start because the orders FK the shop, currency and catalogue rows; the personas become first-class on the host restart the catalogue already requires.

sql.description: Product imagery, one picture PER PRODUCT and a second one to hover onto (#1157). 1.4.0 mapped a tile per SUBGROUP - twelve pictures over ninety-six product rows - and nominated no second image at all, so the PLP card's ShowAlternativeImageOnHover had nothing to swap to. This file now maps the 120 per-product SVGs the layer ships under files/Images/TruvioCommerce/products/ (tc-tile-<concept>-<nnnn> as the default, tc-detail-<concept>-<nnnn> as the second image, both generated by tools/make-tiles.py) onto the 60 masters, with variant rows joined on ProductId so a combination inherits its master's pair. Attached through EcomDetails (column set resolved from sys.columns, since the optional language/sorting/type columns differ across platform builds) and mirrored onto the legacy EcomProducts.ProductImage* columns where the build still has them. The hover row sorts at 1 - ahead of truvio-pdp.sql's gallery rows at 2 and 3 - because Swift takes the FIRST non-default image of the named asset category as the alternative. Converging: the TC-DETAIL-* ids are derived from the product key, so a host seeded at 1.4.0 is updated in place rather than given a second set of rows. A missing EcomDetails table is a loud failure, never a skip, and so are four measured end-state guards: nothing attached, no second image anywhere, two products in one group sharing a default, and a master with fewer than two distinct images. A demo that seeds no image and reports success is the failure this script exists to prevent; a demo that seeds one image five times is the same failure one step later.

The row-level B2B data the PLP and PDP need in order to say anything: a distinct one-sentence short description on all 60 masters, eight to sixteen words, no two in a band opening on the same stem, each naming what THAT product demonstrates rather than what its band does (#1158), guarded by a per-band DISTINCT count and an empty-string count rather than by a row count, a five-step stock profile (healthy / low / zero-but-orderable / mid / deep) with expected-delivery dates and the matching per-location stock-unit rows, 96 REAL customer-group prices scoped to the buyer persona's own AccessUser group so a signed-in figure is visibly below list (marine fakes this: 22 price rows, zero with a user group), a three-step quantity ladder on ten masters rather than the one 1.1.x shipped, and five new contract prices on customer number TC-100200 beside the one the layer already had. Ends in a resolution guard that counts masters priced BELOW list for the persona, because a row count proves nothing about what the page shows.

What fills the product detail page, which the parity report measured at 84 characters of main text with four empty sections. One gallery row per master, DERIVED from that master's own TC-DETAIL default row rather than assigned from a ring: strip the -<nnnn> index off the default's filename and the result is that master's own band concept tile, so a row cannot point at another band's picture (#1137 round three). Three distinct pictures per master - its own tile at sort 0, its own detail image at sort 1, its band tile at sort 2 - and three is the ceiling, which is why the second gallery row is retired rather than repointed - a data layer references no asset outside its own files[]. The photographic set the Distribution's brand/brand-assets.manifest.json declares under scenic/ is an OPTIONAL upgrade applied by tools/truvio-gallery-photos.sql after a brand step has put those five files on disk; it is deliberately undeclared here, because a declared script is one the composer runs and this one would seed 60 404s on any host that skipped the brand step. The Manuals ASSET CATEGORY - one EcomDetailsGroup with extensions pdf, InheritanceType 3 and ControlType 0, the shape Swift's ProductMediaTable binds to when configured ImageAssets=["Manuals"] - carrying 120 document rows over the eight one-page PDFs this layer ships in files/Documents/TruvioCommerce/ and regenerates with tools/make-documents.py. 324 related-product rows in three groups (Related products, Accessories, Spare parts), with the kit story written BOTH ways so a member points back at its kit. And the remaining four category-field values per master, taking every specification table from three rows to seven. Ends in four resolution guards that assert what the page needs - two images, two documents, two relations, exactly seven specification values on every master - rather than what was inserted.
